thread:
devon: Heads up — noticed a spike in cold starts this morning after the Karpenter rollout. GPU pods waiting 40-60s for nodes to register, then immediate eviction churn. Anyone else see this?

cj: yep saw the same in eu-west-1 around 08:12. Pod Pending -> Node Allocated -> Node NotReady -> eviction. Looks like `kubelet` never finished boot before we hit pod eviction threshold.

maria: what are our eviction thresholds set to? I thought we bumped to 2m for gpu workloads?

anya: our default `pod-eviction` is 90s cluster-wide, GPU queue uses a 120s toleration via mutating webhook for priority pods. But some jobs are lower priority and still using 90s.

simon: Important detail: the new Karpenter provisioner uses instance types with slower boot time (p4d in us-west-2) during scaleups due to capacity. Boot time + NV driver install adds ~30s. Combined with networking (dhcp/eni) delays we cross eviction window.

devon: Here's a small snippet from the kubelet logs from one of the affected nodes:```
Aug 09 08:12:34 kubelet[1234]: Starting kubelet
Aug 09 08:12:58 kubelet[1234]: Registering node with apiserver
Aug 09 08:13:10 kubelet[1234]: Pod infrastructure container created
Aug 09 08:13:25 kubelet[1234]: NodeReady
```
so ~51s to NodeReady after process start, and pods were evicted at ~90s threshold.

cj: Do we have `initContainers` that delay scheduling? Also check CNI logs — ENI attachment in some AZs is taking ~20s. If ENI attach + driver install ~=50s, and evict at 90s, any heavy image pull pushes us over.

anya: Two immediate levers: 1) increase eviction threshold for lower-priority GPU pods to 180s (temp). 2) pre-warm nodes or use Karpenter `consolidation=false` to keep hot pool. But pre-warm costs money.

maria: We should also consider switching the provisioner `startupTimeout` and `provider` config to prefer instance types with faster boot for cold path (e.g., g5 vs p4d) and let Karpenter fallback to larger types only when needed. That would reduce cold-start latency.

simon: Also check AMI: our GPU AMI runs a user-data apt install for `nvidia-driver` on boot. We should bake drivers into AMI to save ~20-40s.

devon: Agree — baking drivers + smaller init steps drops node ready time considerably. But we still have ENI limits in some AZs causing retries which Karpenter surfaces as provisioning errors. Any ideas to surface that to the autoscaler?

cj: We can add `NodeTemplate` constraints to avoid AZs hitting ENI quotas under heavy scale. Karpenter supports `topology.kubernetes.io/zone` in constraints. Or use `provisioner.constraints` to prefer less-utilized zones.

anya: Quick cost tradeoff note: pre-warming 5 GPUs per region = ~x$/hr. But reducing evictions avoids requeue/backoff and saves egress and job retry costs. Estimated break-even is ~36 hours for heavy batch workloads.

deploy-bot: [deploy] Canary update of karpenter-provisioner-v2 started at 2026-08-09T08:20:00Z :rocket:

sre-bot: Incident alert: high pod churn in cluster-prod-eu-west-1 between 08:10-08:30 (observed 172 evictions)

maria: Actionable plan:
- bake GPU drivers into AMI (DevOps).
- adjust eviction tolerations for non-critical GPU pods to 180s (Platform).
- add zone preference to karpenter provisioner to avoid saturated AZs (Infra).
- add a small warm pool for high-throughput queues (cost/finance to approve).

cj: I'll open a PR to change the mutating webhook default toleration and a Karpenter provisioner update to add `topologySpread` preference.

devon: I'll prototype a baked AMI and smoke test boot times. If we can shave 30s we might not need warm pool for us-west-2.

anya: Also let's add a short-term metric: `node_boot_time_seconds` (kubelet start -> NodeReady) so we can alert if median > 45s.

simon: For longer-term: consider using mixed-instance types with weighted preference and instance-selector to reduce AZ pressure. Karpenter supports that via `provider.instanceSelector` labels.

maria: Sounds good. Who wants to own the warm-pool cost estimate?

anya: I'll take cost estimate and present to finance by EOD.

devon: Thanks all. Quick wins: AMI bake + toleration bump. I'll post results in this thread after smoke test. :thumbsup:

cj: PTAL at the PR when ready — I'll review.

sre-bot: Note: scheduled job to run cluster-wide eviction-simulation tomorrow 09:00 UTC. Expect transient evictions during test.

devon: Noted. Will avoid running batch jobs during the test window.

maria: Closing loop — will follow-up with rollout plan once AMI bake passes and webhook PR is merged.
